A 80-year-old man with hypertension and a 40-pack-year smoking history (quit 5 years ago) presents
with a painless ulcer at the base of his first toe on his left foot. He reports experiencing left leg pain at
night that improves when his foot hangs off the bed. The ulcer was discovered during routine foot care.
Physical examination reveals the following pulse findings: | Right foot | | | --- | --- | | Femoral | 4+ | |
Popliteal | 3+ | | Dorsalis Pedis | 2+ | | Posterior Tibial | 1+ | | Left foot | | | Femoral | 4+ | | Popliteal | 2+ |
| Dorsalis Pedis | 0 | | Posterior Tibial | 0 | Doppler examination shows decreased flow in the left
posterior tibial artery and no detectable flow in the dorsalis pedis. What is the primary underlying cause
of the patient's toe ulcer? Answer Choices: (A) An occlusion of the deep plantar artery (B) Multiple
small vessel disease of the foot (C) An occlusion of the first dorsal metatarsal artery (D) An occlusion of
the lateral plantar artery (E) Thrombosis of the deep femoral artery (F) An occluded posterior tibial
artery on the left foot (G) An occlusion of the anterior tibial artery (H) A stenosis of the common iliac
artery (I) A narrowing of the superficial femoral artery (J) A stenosis of the popliteal artery bifurcation
 A. An occlusion of the anterior tibial artery
B. A narrowing of the superficial femoral artery
C. A stenosis of the common iliac artery
D. Thrombosis of the deep femoral artery
E. Multiple small vessel disease of the foot
F. An occluded posterior tibial artery on the left foot
G. An occlusion of the lateral plantar artery
H. An occlusion of the first dorsal metatarsal artery
I. A stenosis of the popliteal artery bifurcation
J. An occlusion of the deep plantar artery
